name: querySelectorAll: static list
desc: querySelector returns the first matching element or null. querySelectorAll returns a static NodeList of every match, so it does not update after the page changes.

name: element by id
desc: Finds the element with that id and returns null when no element has it. The id is passed without the # sign, and the method exists only on document.
body: An id such as `room.204` is awkward in a CSS selector, because the dot means a class. `getElementById` takes the raw string and does not parse it, which makes it the safer call when the id comes from data.

name: element.querySelector
desc: Searches only inside the element, not the whole document. Use it when several cards or forms repeat the same inner markup.

name: createElement
desc: Creates a detached element. It is not on the page until you insert it.

name: append, prepend, before, after
desc: append inserts at the end and accepts several nodes and strings. prepend inserts at the start, and before and after insert siblings next to a node.
body:
`appendChild` accepts one node only and returns it. `append` returns nothing and takes any number of arguments.

Appending a node that is already in the document moves it. Clone it when you need a second copy.

name: remove and replaceChildren
desc: remove takes the element out of the document without needing its parent. replaceChildren clears the parent and inserts the new nodes in one call.
body:
A removed node still exists in memory while a variable points at it. Its listeners still run if you keep a reference and dispatch events on it, but the user cannot see it and CSS no longer applies.

`removeChild(child)` throws when the node is not a child of that parent. `remove()` has no such failure mode.

name: safe text vs parsed HTML
desc: textContent writes plain text and is safe for user input. innerHTML parses markup, and injected attributes such as onerror can run script.
body:
`innerHTML +=` re-parses the whole subtree and replaces every child. Listeners on the old children are lost, and variables holding them point at detached nodes.

`innerText` reads rendered text and forces layout. Use `textContent` unless the visible text, with line breaks and hidden elements, is what you need.

name: classList methods
desc: Adds, removes, toggles, replaces, and tests classes one at a time. Assigning className replaces every class on the element.
body:
`toggle` takes a second argument that forces the state:

```js
card.classList.toggle("is-hidden", !matches);
```

SVG elements expose `className` as an object, not a string, so `classList` is the portable choice.

name: style and getComputedStyle
desc: style edits inline CSS. Dash names become camelCase properties, or use setProperty. getComputedStyle returns the resolved value that applies.
body:
Reading `panel.style.width` returns only the inline value, an empty string when the width comes from a stylesheet.

Prefer a class for a named state. Inline styles beat stylesheet rules, so a forgotten inline value is hard to override later.

name: getAttribute and setAttribute
desc: Attributes are strings. getAttribute returns null when the attribute is missing, and a boolean attribute such as disabled works by presence, not by value.
body:
`setAttribute("disabled", "false")` still disables the control. Remove the attribute to enable it.

A property such as `checked` is the live state. The attribute `checked` is the default state, and changing it does not change what the user sees.

name: dataset
desc: Reads and writes data-* attributes as camelCase keys. Every value is a string, including numbers you assign.
example:
// <li data-hotel-id="42" data-city="Budapest">
const item = document.querySelector("li");

console.log(item.dataset.hotelId);          // "42"
console.log(Number(item.dataset.hotelId) + 1); // 43

item.dataset.stars = 4;   // writes data-stars="4"
delete item.dataset.city; // removes data-city

console.log(item.getAttribute("data-stars")); // "4"
body:
HTML lowercases attribute names. `data-hotelId` in markup becomes `data-hotelid`, which does not match `dataset.hotelId`. Write kebab case in HTML and camelCase in JavaScript.

After `delete`, the key reads as `undefined`, not `null`.

name: reading form controls
desc: Reads control state. Text values are always strings, checkboxes and radios use checked, and a select exposes value plus selectedOptions.
body:
`form.elements` allows lookup by name, and a name that collides with a form property such as `submit` shadows it. Choose field names that cannot collide with the form API.

Radio buttons with the same name form a group. `form.elements.rooms.value` returns the checked value or an empty string.

name: FormData: collect fields
desc: Collects successful controls as key and value pairs. Disabled fields, unchecked checkboxes, and the submit button are skipped.

name: constraint validation
desc: Constraint checks live on input.validity. Clear a custom message with an empty string, then check or report the form.
body:
The browser blocks the `submit` event while a constraint fails. Your own submit handler will not run for an invalid form unless the form has `novalidate`. That is a common exam trick: a handler that seems broken is simply never called.

`setCustomValidity("")` clears the error. Forgetting the empty call leaves the field permanently invalid.

name: addEventListener options
desc: The third argument controls capture, once, passive, and an abort signal. Removal needs the same function and the same capture flag.
body:
`passive: true` promises not to call `preventDefault`, which lets the browser scroll without waiting. A `preventDefault` inside a passive listener is ignored.

Adding the same function twice for the same type and capture flag does nothing. Different `once` or `passive` values do not create a second listener.

name: event object fields
desc: Each dispatch creates one event object. target is where the event started, currentTarget is the node running the current listener.
body:
`currentTarget` is set to `null` after dispatch finishes, so do not read it inside a timeout. Store `event.target` in a variable if the value is needed later.

Keyboard events add `key`, `code`, `repeat`, and the modifier booleans. Submit events add `submitter`.

name: bubbling and capture
desc: Capture runs from the root down, then the target handler runs, then the event bubbles back up. focus, blur, mouseenter, mouseleave, load, and scroll on an element do not bubble.
body:
Use `focusin` and `focusout` for focus delegation, because `focus` and `blur` do not bubble. `mouseover` and `mouseout` bubble where `mouseenter` and `mouseleave` do not.

A capturing listener is the only way to observe a non-bubbling event on an ancestor.

name: event delegation with closest
desc: One listener on a stable parent handles current rows and rows created later. closest walks up from the real click target to the matching element.
body:
Delegation survives re-rendering. A listener attached to each row is lost as soon as the row is replaced, which is the usual cause of a button that works once.

Guard the case where `closest` returns `null`, and keep the selector narrow so a click in the container itself does not match.

name: stopPropagation and stopImmediatePropagation
desc: stops the event from moving to the next node. It does not cancel the browser default action, which is preventDefault. Immediate also skips the remaining listeners on the current node.
body:
A `stopPropagation` call on a link does not stop the navigation. Use `preventDefault` for that, and check `event.cancelable` when the event may not support cancellation.

Order the checks inside one delegated listener before reaching for propagation control. It is easier to follow and cannot silently break other features.

name: preventDefault
desc: Cancels the browser default for a cancelable event. A non-cancelable event ignores the call, and a passive listener cannot use it.
body:
`preventDefault` must run during dispatch. Calling it after the handler returns, for example inside a timeout, changes nothing.

Check `event.defaultPrevented` when another part of the page may already have cancelled the action.

name: input and change
desc: input fires on every value change, including paste and drop. change fires when the user commits: on blur for text, immediately for checkbox, radio, select, and date fields.
body:
Use `input` for live feedback and `change` for an action that should run once per decision.

A debounce timer stops an expensive filter from running on every keystroke. The composition guard keeps a half-typed Japanese or Chinese word from being searched.

name: submit
desc: Fires on the form for a submit button click and for Enter in a single-line field. An invalid form blocks the event unless the form has novalidate.
body:
A button inside a form defaults to `type="submit"`. A button that must only run script needs `type="button"`.

Pressing Enter in a `textarea` inserts a newline and does not submit, so a chat-style editor can live inside a form safely.

name: keydown and event.key
desc: keydown fires when a key goes down and repeats while it is held. key is the character or name, code is the physical key, and the modifier booleans cover Ctrl, Alt, Shift, and Meta.
body:
`event.key` values include `"Enter"`, `"Escape"`, `"ArrowLeft"`, `" "` for space, and `"a"` or `"A"` depending on Shift. `event.code` values include `"KeyA"`, `"Space"`, and `"Digit1"`.

`event.repeat` is true for the repeated events while a key is held, which is useful for scrolling a list and wrong for toggling a dialog.

`keypress` is deprecated. `keyCode` is deprecated and layout dependent.
